Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."

value.zh: 既而中宮凶忍，久懷危害之心，外戚諂諛，競進讒邪之說；
value.en: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.
value.literal: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.

value.zh: 坎牲之謀已構，斃犬之譖遂行；
value.en: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.
value.literal: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.

value.zh: 一人乏探隱之聰，百辟無爭臣之節。
value.en: The ruler lacked the discernment to uncover hidden matters, and the ministers lacked the integrity to remonstrate.
value.literal: Thus one man lacked keen insight into hidden matters; the hundred ministers showed no temper of remonstrating subjects.

value.zh: 遂使冤逾楚建，酷甚戾園。
value.en: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.
value.literal: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.

value.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！
value.en: Posthumous honors could not resurrect him.
value.literal: Though mourning rites ran full and grief ran deep, what did they mend for the poisoned innocent!

value.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
value.en: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.
value.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.

value.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
value.en: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.
value.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.

value.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
value.en: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.
value.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.

value.zh: 掇蜂構隙，歸胙生災。
value.en: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.
value.literal: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.

value.zh: 既罹凶忍，徒望歸來。
value.en: Death ended every hope of restoration.
value.literal: Once brutal cruelty struck, vain hope alone remained of return.

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 溫嶠
value.en: Wen Jiao.
value.literal: Wen Jiao.

value.zh: 永昌初，徵拜領軍將軍，既至，轉尚書，以疾不拜。
value.en: Early in Yongchang he was recalled as colonel of the guards; transferred to secretary but declined on grounds of illness.
value.literal: At the beginning of Yongchang he was summoned as Colonel of the Garrison Army; having arrived, he was transferred to Secretary—because of illness he did not accept.

value.zh: 時明帝初即位，王敦專制，內外危逼，謀杖鑒為外援，由是拜安西將軍、兗州刺史、都督揚州江西諸軍、假節，鎮合肥。
value.en: Emperor Ming faced Wang Dun's dictatorship and stationed Xi Jian west as general who pacifies the west, inspector of Yanzhou, area commander from the Yangzi westward—with credential and headquarters at Hefei.
value.literal: At the time Emperor Ming had newly ascended; Wang Dun monopolized power; internal and external peril pressed—the plot leaned on Jian as outer support; therefore he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yanzhou, Area Commander of Jiangxi military affairs south of Yangzhou, acting credential, garrisoned at Hefei.

value.zh: 敦忌之，表為尚書令，徵還。
value.en: Wang Dun envied him and engineered his recall as director of state affairs.
value.literal: Dun envied him and memorialized him as Director of the Department of State Affairs, summoning him back.

value.zh: 道經姑孰，與敦相見，敦謂曰：「樂彥輔短才耳。
value.en: At Gushu Wang Dun sneered, "Yue Guang is second-rate.
value.literal: Passing through Gushu he met Dun; Dun said to him: "Yue Yanfu is but minor talent.

value.zh: 後生流宕，言違名檢，考之以實，豈勝滿武秋邪？」
value.en: Those gifted youngsters break every rule—tell me how Yue Guang outranks Man Yi."
value.literal: Later youths drift dissolute; speech violates name and scrutiny—examining by facts, how could he surpass Man Wuqiu?

value.zh: 鑒曰：「擬人必于其倫。
value.en: Xi Jian replied, "Compare like with like.
value.literal: Jian said: "When comparing men one must match kind.

value.zh: 彥輔道韻平淡，體識沖粹，處傾危之朝，不可得而親疏。
value.en: Yue Guang moves through a dangerous court with serene detachment—neither push nor pull him off balance.
value.literal: Yanfu's Dao charm is placid and plain; his substance and insight are limpid and pure; in a tottering court one cannot draw him near or push him far.

value.zh: 及愍懷太子之廢，可謂柔而有正。
value.en: When they cashiered Crown Prince Minhuai he remained gentle yet principled.
value.literal: At the deposition of Crown Prince Minhuai he may be called yielding yet upright.

value.zh: 武秋失節之士，何可同日而言！」
value.en: Man Yi broke his oath—no comparison."
value.literal: Wuqiu is a man who lost integrity—how may they be spoken of the same day!

value.zh: 敦曰：「愍懷廢徙之際，交有危機之急，人何能以死守之乎！
value.en: Wang Dun shot back, "During that crisis who could die on principle?
value.literal: Dun said: "At the deposition and exile of Minhuai, mutually there was crisis acute—how could men guard it with death!

value.zh: 以此相方，其不減明矣。」
value.en: Then Yue Guang shines brighter."
value.literal: Using this to compare squarely, his inferiority is clear.

value.zh: 鑒曰：「丈夫既潔身北面，義同在三，豈可偷生屈節，靦顏天壤邪！
value.en: Xi Jian said, "A man who serves the throne upholds the three bonds—he does not cling to life and betray honor.
value.literal: Jian said: "A gentleman having purified himself to serve the north face, duty joins the Three Bonds—how may he steal life and bend his integrity, shame-faced between Heaven and earth!

value.zh: 苟道數終極，固當存亡以之耳。」
value.en: When fate ends, you accept survival or ruin with it."
value.literal: If the Dao's reckoning reaches its end, indeed one should live or die by it.

value.zh: 敦素懷無君之心，聞鑒言，大忿之，遂不復相見，拘留不遣。
value.en: Wang Dun—who already disdained emperors—raged at that speech, refused further audiences, and held Xi Jian hostage.
value.literal: Dun always harbored a heart without a lord; hearing Jian's words he greatly resented him; then would no longer meet him and detained him without sending him away.

value.zh: 敦之黨與譖毀日至，鑒舉止自若，初無懼心。
value.en: While Wang Dun's clique daily maligned him, Xi Jian stayed calm and afraid of nothing.
value.literal: Dun's faction daily spread slander; Jian's bearing remained composed—at first no fear.

value.zh: 敦謂錢鳳曰：「郗道徽儒雅之士，名位既重，何得害之！」
value.en: He told Qian Feng, "Xi Jian is a scholar of stature—we cannot murder him."
value.literal: Dun said to Qian Feng: "Xi Daohui is a Confucian gentleman; name and position are already weighty—how could we harm him!

value.zh: 乃放還臺。
value.en: He released Xi Jian to return to the capital.
value.literal: Thereupon he was released to return to the metropolitan apparatus.

value.zh: 鑒遂與帝謀滅敦。
value.en: Xi Jian then joined Emperor Ming to plot Wang Dun's destruction.
value.literal: Jian thereupon with the emperor plotted to destroy Dun.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

value.zh: 太子幼有令名，及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲。
value.en: The heir apparent had a good name as a child, but as he grew he neglected study and played only with his attendants.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent in youth had a fine reputation; when he grew up he did not love learning and only played with those at his side.

value.zh: 賈后復使黃門輩誘之為奢靡威虐，由是名譽浸減，驕慢益彰。
value.en: Empress Jia also set Yellow Gate attendants to lure him into extravagance and cruelty. His reputation faded and his arrogance grew.
value.literal: Empress Jia again had the Yellow Gate attendants entice him into extravagance and cruel arrogance; thereby his reputation gradually declined and his insolence grew more manifest.

value.zh: 或廢朝侍而縱游逸，於宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。
value.en: He sometimes skipped court to roam freely, opened a market inside the palace, had men butcher meat and sell wine, and weighed goods himself without missing by an ounce.
value.literal: He sometimes skipped court attendance to roam in idleness, set up a market within the palace, had men butcher and sell wine, and weighed goods in his own hand without error in light and heavy.

value.zh: 其母，本屠家女也，故太子好之。
value.en: His mother had been a butcher's daughter, which is why he took to such pursuits.
value.literal: His mother had originally been a butcher's daughter, and therefore the Heir Apparent delighted in such things.

value.zh: 東宮月俸錢五十萬，太子常探取二月，用之猶不足。
value.en: The Eastern Palace received five hundred thousand cash a month, yet he often drew two months' stipend at once and still found it insufficient.
value.literal: The Eastern Palace's monthly stipend was five hundred thousand cash; the Heir Apparent often drew two months' worth at once and still found it insufficient.

value.zh: 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面等物而收其利。
value.en: He also had the Western Garden sell vegetables, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and other goods for profit.
value.literal: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like and collect the profit.

value.zh: 又好陰陽小數，多所拘忌。
value.en: He was also fond of yin-yang lore and petty numerology and observed many taboos.
value.literal: He also loved yin-yang lore and petty numerology and was much bound by taboos.

value.zh: 洗馬江統上書陳五事：「一曰雖有微苦，宜力疾朝侍。
value.en: Jiang Tong, Groom of the Heir Apparent, memorialized with five recommendations: "First, though you are slightly unwell, you should force yourself to attend court.
value.literal: The Groom of the Heir Apparent, Jiang Tong, submitted a memorial setting forth five points: "First, though there is slight illness, you ought to force yourself to attend court.

value.zh: 二曰宜勤見保傅，咨讒善道。
value.en: Second, you should often consult your tutors and seek the path of virtue.
value.literal: Second, you ought diligently to see your tutors and consult them on the good path.

value.zh: 三曰畫室之功，可且減省，後園刻鏤雜作，一皆罷遣。
value.en: Third, cut back on the painting studios and dismiss all carved and inlaid work in the rear garden.
value.literal: Third, the work of the painting studios may for now be reduced; carved and inlaid miscellaneous tasks in the rear garden should all be dismissed.

value.zh: 四曰西園賣葵、藍之屬，虧敗國體，貶損令聞。
value.en: Fourth, selling vegetables and indigo from the Western Garden disgraces the state and harms your reputation.
value.literal: Fourth, selling mallow, indigo, and the like in the Western Garden damages the state's dignity and lowers your fine reputation.

value.zh: 五曰繕牆正瓦，不必拘攣小忌。」
value.en: Fifth, when repairing walls and resetting tiles, you need not be bound by petty taboos."
value.literal: Fifth, when repairing walls and straightening tiles, you need not be bound by petty taboos."

value.zh: 太子皆不從。
value.en: The heir apparent ignored every point.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent would not follow any of them.

value.zh: 中舍人杜錫，恐太子不得安其位，每盡忠諫，勸太子修德業，保令名，言辭懇切。
value.en: Du Xi, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, fearing the heir apparent might lose his position, repeatedly urged him in loyal remonstrance to cultivate virtue and preserve his good name, his words earnest and forceful.
value.literal: Du Xi, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, fearing the Heir Apparent could not secure his position, each time offered loyal remonstrance, urging the Heir Apparent to cultivate virtue and preserve his fine name, his words earnest.

value.zh: 太子患之，置針著錫常所坐氈中，刺之流血，錫，預之子也。
value.en: The heir apparent resented this, hid needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent resented this, placed needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.

value.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃中宮驕貴，不能假借之。
value.en: The heir apparent was proud by nature. Knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent was by nature stern; knowing that Jia Mi relied on the central palace's arrogant eminence, he could not show him favor.

value.zh: 謐時為侍中，至東宮，或捨之，於後庭遊戲。
value.en: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate. When he visited the Eastern Palace the heir apparent sometimes dismissed him and amused himself in the rear court.
value.literal: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate; when he came to the Eastern Palace the Heir Apparent sometimes dismissed him and played in the rear court.

value.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「謐，后所親暱，一旦交構，則事危矣。」
value.en: Steward Pei Quan warned him: "Mi is the empress's favorite. If you quarrel with him, disaster will follow."
value.literal: The Steward Pei Quan remonstrated: "Mi is one the empress cherishes; if you should clash, the affair would be perilous."

value.zh: 不從。
value.en: He would not listen.
value.literal: He did not heed him.

value.zh: 謐譖太子於后曰：「太子多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
value.en: Mi slandered the heir apparent to the empress, saying: "He hoards private wealth to win over petty men because he means to destroy the Jia clan.
value.literal: Mi slandered the Heir Apparent to the empress, saying: "The Heir Apparent amasses private wealth to win over petty men because of the Jia clan.

value.zh: 若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等，廢后於金墉，如反手耳。
value.en: When the emperor dies and he takes the throne, he will follow the Yang clan precedent, execute us, and imprison you at Jinyong. It will be as easy as turning his hand.
value.literal: If the imperial carriage should halt forever and he take the great position, following the Yang clan precedent he would execute us ministers and depose the empress at Jinyong—it would be like turning the hand.

value.zh: 不如早圖之，更立慈順者，可以自安。」
value.en: Better act early and set up another heir who is mild and obedient. Then we may be safe."
value.literal: Better to plot early, set up another who is kindly and obedient, and thus secure ourselves."

value.zh: 后納其言，乃宣揚太子之短，佈於遠近。
value.en: The empress accepted his counsel and spread the heir apparent's faults far and wide.
value.literal: The empress accepted his words and thereupon spread abroad the Heir Apparent's faults, broadcasting them far and near.

value.zh: 又詐為有娠，內蒿物、產具，取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，欲以代太子。
value.en: She also feigned pregnancy, hid birthing supplies inside, took her brother-in-law Han Shou's son Weizu to rear, and planned to replace the heir apparent with him.
value.literal: She also feigned pregnancy, hid artemisia and birthing gear within, took her brother-in-law Han Shou's son Weizu to rear, and intended to replace the Heir Apparent with him.

value.zh: 十二月，太子長子虨病，太子為虨求王爵，不許。
value.en: In the twelfth month the heir apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill. The heir apparent asked that he be made a prince, but the request was denied.
value.literal: In the twelfth month the Heir Apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill; the Heir Apparent sought a princely title for Xian but was not granted it.

value.zh: 虨疾篤，太子為之禱祀求福。
value.en: As Xian grew gravely ill, the heir apparent prayed and offered sacrifices on his behalf.
value.literal: When Xian's illness grew grave, the Heir Apparent prayed and offered sacrifices to seek blessing for him.

value.zh: 賈后聞之，乃詐稱帝不豫，召太子入朝，既至，后不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞以帝命賜太子酒三升，使盡飲之。
value.en: Empress Jia heard of this and falsely announced that the emperor was ill, summoning the heir apparent to court. When he arrived she refused to see him, placed him in a side room, and sent the maid Chen Wu with the emperor's name to give him three pints of wine and order him to drink it all.
value.literal: When Empress Jia heard of it she falsely announced the emperor was unwell and summoned the Heir Apparent to court; once he arrived the empress did not see him but placed him in a separate room and sent the maid Chen Wu, in the emperor's name, to bestow three pints of wine on the Heir Apparent and order him to drink it all.

value.zh: 太子辭以不能飲三升，舞逼之曰：「不孝邪！
value.en: He declined, saying he could not drink so much. Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial?
value.literal: The Heir Apparent declined, saying he could not drink three pints; Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial!

value.zh: 天賜汝酒而不飲，酒中有惡物邪！」
value.en: Heaven grants you wine and you refuse. Do you think it poisoned?"
value.literal: Heaven bestows wine upon you and you will not drink—is there something evil in the wine!"

value.zh: 太子不得已，強飲至盡，遂大醉。
value.en: Unable to refuse further, he drank it all and became thoroughly drunk.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent had no choice, forced himself to drink to the end, and became very drunk.

value.zh: 后使黃門侍朗潘岳作書草，令小婢承福，以紙筆及草，因太子醉，稱詔使書之，文曰：「陛下宜自了，不自了，吾當入了之。
value.en: The empress had Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Attendant, draft a letter and sent the maid Cheng Fu with paper, brush, and draft. While the heir apparent was drunk she claimed an imperial order and made him copy it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle this yourself. If you do not, I shall enter and settle it.
value.literal: The empress had the Yellow Gate Attendant Pan Yue draft a letter, ordered the little maid Cheng Fu to bring paper, brush, and draft; taking advantage of the Heir Apparent's drunkenness she claimed an edict and made him write it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle matters yourself; if you do not settle them, I shall enter and settle them.

value.zh: 中宮又宜速自了，不自了，吾當手了之。
value.en: The empress too ought quickly to settle matters herself. If she does not, I shall settle them with my own hand.
value.literal: The central palace too ought quickly to settle matters herself; if she does not, I shall settle them with my own hand.

value.zh: 並與謝妃共要，刻期兩發，勿疑猶豫，以致後患。
value.en: I have agreed with Consort Xie. We have set a date for both to act. Do not hesitate and bring later trouble.
value.literal: Together with Consort Xie we have agreed; set a date for both to act—do not doubt or hesitate and bring later trouble.

value.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣氏為內主。
value.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood under heaven. August Heaven has promised to sweep away the harm, establish Daowen as king, and make the Jiang clan the inner mistress.
value.literal: Eating raw flesh and drinking blood beneath the three luminaries—August Heaven has promised to sweep away the harm, establish Daowen as king, and make the Jiang clan the inner mistress.

value.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君。」
value.en: When it succeeds, we shall offer the three sacrificial beasts to the Northern Lord."
value.literal: When the wish is fulfilled, we shall offer the three sacrificial beasts to the Northern Lord."

value.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之。
value.en: Drunk and unaware, he copied it as dictated.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent, drunk and dazed and unaware, thereupon copied it as given.

value.zh: 其字半不成，后補成之，以呈帝。
value.en: Half the characters were incomplete. The empress finished them and presented the letter to the emperor.
value.literal: Half his characters were incomplete; the empress completed them and presented it to the emperor.

value.zh: 壬戌，帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛以太子書及青紙詔示之曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
value.en: On the day renxu the emperor went to the Shiqian Hall and summoned the ministers. Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng showed them the heir apparent's letter and a blue-paper edict, saying: "Yu wrote this. He is to die."
value.literal: On the day renxu the emperor visited the Shiqian Hall, summoned the excellencies and ministers in, and had the Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng show them the Heir Apparent's letter and the blue-paper edict, saying: "Yu's letter is thus—now grant death."

value.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者。
value.en: He showed it to all the princes and nobles. No one spoke.
value.literal: He showed it to all the princes and lords; none spoke.

value.zh: 張華曰：「此國之大禍，自古以來，常因廢黜正嫡以致喪亂。
value.en: Zhang Hua said, "This is a great calamity for the state. Since antiquity disorder has often followed the deposition of the legitimate heir.
value.literal: Zhang Hua said: "This is a great calamity for the state. Since antiquity disorder has often come from deposing the legitimate heir.

value.zh: 且國家有天下日淺，願陛下詳之！」
value.en: Moreover the dynasty has held the realm only a short time. I beg Your Majesty to consider carefully!"
value.literal: Moreover the state has held the realm but a short time—I beg Your Majesty to consider carefully!"

value.zh: 裴頠以為宜先檢校傳書者，又請比較太子手書，不然，恐有詐妄。
value.en: Pei Wei urged that the messenger be examined first and the handwriting compared with the heir apparent's own script, lest the letter be a forgery.
value.literal: Pei Wei held that one ought first to examine and verify the person who transmitted the letter, and also requested comparison with the Heir Apparent's own handwriting; otherwise he feared there might be fraud.

value.zh: 賈后乃出太子啟事十餘紙，眾人比視，亦無敢言非者。
value.en: Empress Jia then produced more than ten sheets of the heir apparent's memorials. When the assembly compared them, no one dared say they did not match.
value.literal: Empress Jia then produced more than ten sheets of the Heir Apparent's memorials; when the assembly compared them, none dared say they did not match.

value.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各不同，其不從詔者，宜以軍法從事。」
value.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng report to the emperor in the name of the Princess of Changguang: "This must be decided at once. The ministers are divided. Those who disobey the edict should be dealt with by military law."
value.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng, falsely in the name of the Princess of Changguang, report to the emperor: "The affair ought to be decided quickly, yet the ministers all differ; those who do not follow the edict ought to be handled by military law."

value.zh: 議至日西，不決。
value.en: Debate continued until sunset without resolution.
value.literal: Deliberation continued until the sun was in the west, without decision.

value.zh: 后見華等意堅，懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
value.en: Seeing Zhang Hua and the others hold firm and fearing the plot might fail, the empress memorialized to depose the heir apparent as a commoner. The edict was approved.
value.literal: The empress, seeing that Hua and the others were firm in intent and fearing the affair might change, submitted a memorial to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner; an edict approved it.

value.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
value.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Marquis of Chewu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
value.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Marquis of Chewu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

value.zh: 王衍自表離婚，許之，妃慟哭而歸。
value.en: Wang Yan memorialized to divorce her, and permission was granted. The consort returned home in bitter tears.
value.literal: Wang Yan himself submitted a memorial requesting divorce; it was granted, and the consort returned home weeping bitterly.

value.zh: 殺太子母謝淑媛及虨母保林蔣俊。
value.en: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Xian's mother, Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were executed.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Xian's mother, the Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were killed.

value.zh: 西戎校尉司馬閻纘輿棺詣闕上書，以為：「漢戾太子稱兵拒命，言者猶曰罪當笞耳。
value.en: Yan Xun, Major under the Colonel of the Western Rong, came to the palace gate with his coffin on a cart and submitted a memorial, arguing: "When Emperor Wu's heir apparent Liu Ju took up arms in rebellion, critics still said his offense deserved only a beating.
value.literal: Yan Xun, Major of the Colonel of the Western Rong, came to the gate with his coffin on a cart and submitted a memorial, holding: "When the Han Heir Apparent Li raised troops and defied orders, those who spoke still said his crime merited only the bastinado.

value.zh: 今遹受罪之日，不敢失道，猶為輕於戾太子。
value.en: Now Yu stands condemned yet has not strayed from duty; even so his case is still treated more leniently than that of Crown Prince Li.
value.literal: Now on the day Yu received punishment he did not dare stray from the Way, yet this is still lighter than the Heir Apparent Li.

value.zh: 宜重選師傅，先加嚴誨，若不悛改，棄之未晚也。」書奏，不省。
value.en: The court should appoint new tutors and admonish him strictly. If he does not reform, deposing him would not yet be too late." The memorial was submitted, but it was not examined.
value.literal: One ought to choose tutors anew and first apply stern instruction; if he does not repent and reform, to discard him would not be too late." The memorial was submitted, but it was not examined.

value.zh: 纘，圃之孫也。
value.en: Xun was the grandson of Yan Pu.
value.literal: Xun was the grandson of Yan Pu.

value.zh: 詔追復故太子遹位號，使尚書和郁帥東宮官屬迎太子喪於許昌，追封遹子虨為南陽王，封虨弟臧為臨淮王，尚為襄陽王。
value.en: An edict restored Yu's title, sent He Yu to bring the coffin from Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Xian as Prince of Nanyang and brothers Zang and Shang as princes.
value.literal: An edict restored the former Heir Apparent Yu's title and rank, sent the Masters of Writing He Yu leading Eastern Palace officials to meet the Heir Apparent's coffin at Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Yu's son Xian as Prince of Nanyang, and enfeoffed Xian's brothers Zang as Prince of Linhuai and Shang as Prince of Xiangyang.

value.zh: 相國倫欲收入望，選用海內名德之士，以前平陽太守李重、滎陽太守荀組為左、右長史，東平王堪、沛國劉謨為左、右司馬，尚書郎陽平束皙為記室，淮南王文學荀嵩、殿中郎陸機為參軍。
value.en: Lun sought esteem and recruited renowned men: Li Chong and Xun Zu as chief clerks; Kan, Prince of Dongping, and Liu Mo as majors; Shuxi as recorder; Xun Song and Lu Ji on staff.
value.literal: Chancellor Lun wished to win esteem and selected men of virtue throughout the realm: the former Administrator of Pingyang Li Chong and Administrator of Xingyang Xun Zu as Left and Right Chief Clerks; the Prince of Dongping Kan and Liu Mo of Peiguo as Left and Right Majors; Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Shuxi of Yangping as Recorder; the Literary Scholar of Huainan Xun Song and Palace Gentleman Lu Ji as Staff.

value.zh: 組，勖之子；
value.en: Zu was the son of Xun Xu;
value.literal: Zu was the son of Xun Xu;

value.zh: 嵩，彧之玄孫也。
value.en: Song was the great-great-grandson of Xun Yu.
value.literal: Song was the great-great-grandson of Xun Yu.

value.zh: 李重知倫有異志，辭疾不就，倫逼之不已，憂憤成疾，扶曳受拜，數日而卒。
value.en: Li Chong saw Lun's rebellious intent, pleaded illness, was forced to accept office, and died within days of grief.
value.literal: Li Chong knew Lun harbored rebellious intent, declined illness and would not come; Lun pressed him without cease; he fell ill from grief and anger, was carried in to accept appointment, and died within days.

value.zh: 太子遹之廢也，將立淮南王允為太弟，議者不合。
value.en: When Yu was deposed they considered making Yun, Prince of Huainan, heir younger brother; deliberators disagreed.
value.literal: When the Heir Apparent Yu was deposed, they were about to establish the Prince of Huainan Yun as heir younger brother; deliberators did not agree.

value.zh: 會趙王倫廢賈后，乃以允為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，領中護軍。
value.en: When Lun deposed the empress, Yun was made General of Agile Cavalry with Three Excellencies privilege and Central Protector.
value.literal: When the Prince of Zhao Lun deposed Empress Jia, Yun was made General of Agile Cavalry with privilege as the Three Excellencies and Commander of the Central Protector of the Army.

value.zh: 己卯，謚故太子曰愍懷；
value.en: On jimao the former heir apparent received the posthumous title Minhuai;
value.literal: On the day jimao the former Heir Apparent was given the posthumous title Minhuai;

value.zh: 六月，壬寅，葬於顯平陵。
value.en: In the sixth month, on renyin, he was buried at Xianping Tomb.
value.literal: In the sixth month, on the day renyin, he was buried at Xianping Tomb.

value.zh: 資治通鑑巻第二百一十四
value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214

value.zh: 上之爲臨淄王也，趙麗妃、皇甫德儀、劉才人皆有寵，麗妃生太子瑛，德儀生鄂王瑤，才人生光王琚。
value.en: As Prince of Linzi he had favored Consort Zhao Lifi, Consort Huangfu Deyi, and Lady Liu; Lifi bore Crown Prince Ying, Deyi bore Prince E Yao, and Lady Liu bore Prince Guang Ju.
value.literal: When the Emperor had been Prince of Linzi, Consort Zhao Lifi, Consort Huangfu Deyi, and Lady Liu the Talented were all favored; Lifi bore Crown Prince Ying, Deyi bore Prince E Yao, and the Talented Lady bore Prince Guang Ju.

value.zh: 及即位，幸武惠妃，麗妃等愛皆馳；
value.en: After enthronement he favored Consort Wu Huifei, and the others waned in favor;
value.literal: After his accession he favored Consort Wu Huifei, and affection for Lifi and the others slackened;

value.zh: 惠妃生壽王瑁，寵冠諸子。
value.en: Huifei bore Prince Shou Li Mao, favored above all other sons.
value.literal: Huifei bore Prince Shou Mao, whose favor surpassed all other sons.

value.zh: 太子與瑤、琚會於内第，各以母失職有怨望語。
value.en: The Crown Prince met Yao and Ju privately, each venting resentment over his mother's fall from favor.
value.literal: The Crown Prince met with Yao and Ju in the inner quarters, each speaking resentfully of his mother's loss of favor.

value.zh: 駙馬都尉楊洄尚咸宜公主，常伺三子過失以告惠妃。
value.en: Commandant of Cavaliers Yang Hui, married to Princess Xianyi, constantly watched the three princes' missteps and reported them to Consort Wu Huifei.
value.literal: Commandant of Cavaliers Yang Hui, who had married Princess Xianyi, constantly watched the three sons' faults and reported them to Huifei.

value.zh: 惠妃泣訴於上曰：「太子陰結黨與，將害妾母子，亦指斥至尊。」
value.en: Consort Wu Huifei tearfully told the Emperor: "The Crown Prince is secretly building a faction and plotting to destroy me and my son—and he even rails against Your Majesty himself."
value.literal: Consort Wu Huifei, weeping, complained to the Emperor, saying: "The Crown Prince has secretly formed a faction and will harm me and my son; he also insults Your Majesty."

value.zh: 上大怒，以語宰相，欲皆廢之。
value.en: The Emperor flew into a rage, told his chief ministers what she said, and declared he would remove all three princes.
value.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered; he told the chief ministers and wished to depose them all.

value.zh: 九齡曰：「陛下踐祚垂三十年，太子諸王不離深宮，日受聖訓，天下之人皆慶陛下享國久長，子孫蕃昌。
value.en: Zhang Jiuling replied: "Your Majesty has ruled for nearly thirty years. The Crown Prince and the royal princes have never left the inner palace; day after day they receive your instruction. All the realm rejoices that your reign will be long and your line will flourish.
value.literal: Zhang Jiuling said: "Your Majesty has occupied the throne for nearly thirty years; the Crown Prince and the princes have not left the inner palace, receiving the sage's instruction daily—all under Heaven rejoice that Your Majesty will long hold the state and that descendants will flourish in abundance.

value.zh: 今三子皆已成人，不聞大過，陛下奈何一旦以無根之語，喜怒之際，盡廢之乎！
value.en: All three are grown men now, and no serious wrongdoing has been reported. How can you, on the spur of anger, act on unsubstantiated gossip and disinherit them all at once!
value.literal: Now all three sons have already become adults, and no great faults are heard—how can Your Majesty, in a moment of passion over baseless words, depose them all!

value.zh: 且太子天下本，不可輕搖。
value.en: Besides, the Crown Prince is the very foundation of the realm. That foundation must not be casually undermined.
value.literal: Moreover, the Crown Prince is the root of all under Heaven—it must not be lightly shaken.
